description: What the swarm has actually run against an approach. An approach counts as attempted only when it appears here. Append one entry per run; never edit past entries. outcome: completed (decisive artifact produced and logged, pass or fail), partial (some of the decisive result), abandoned (stopped without it), in-progress. settled: true if the completed result settled its target (the problem or the piece the approach names), false if not, null if unknown or not completed. Fields: approach (id), problem (id, optional if approach is given), date (YYYY-MM-DD), outcome, settled, solves_problem (true only if the logged artifacts meet the problem's acceptance criteria or hit a falsifier), artifact (path to the Lean report, claim-test result or file, relative to ), note. Optional: agent (model slug of the agent that ran it, null if the report does not record one), claims (claim ids the run bears on), test (claim-test result.json the run produced, relative to ), report (the run report). Each entry becomes a delphir:run nanopub (problems/build/build-nanopubs.mjs).

runs.note: The Coleman random-placement null was computed on 1,618 feasible grid cells (lognormal, log-series and Preston canonical pools): median null z 0.134, 5th to 95th percentile 0 to 0.925, 7.0% of cells in [0.20, 0.30]; total abundance J explains 79% of the null variance. The comparison with observed exponents was not run: the Triantis, Guilhaumon and Whittaker 2012 compilation is closed and no open copy was found. Claim-level verdict inconclusive (data-unavailable). The approach's own failure signature holds: with J free the null sits almost anywhere in (0, 1), so it does not discriminate.

Adapted: a logseries-placement null calibrated on Borneo (S = 7,534) with individuals per km2 as a free nuisance parameter, scored against 1,123 GIFT islands (empirical pooled z = 0.307). On the pre-registered density grid (10 to 1e8 per km2) the 95% null interval never contains the empirical z, so the pre-registered outcome is failed. A post hoc fine sweep shows the null's z spans 0.07 to 0.81 with density, matching 0.307 at about 2.9e4 per km2: the null is not constraining, and sampling is neither confirmed nor ruled out as the source of the exponent.

Pre-registered (PREREG.md, sha256 6573bfe3) and run on GIFT: 1,124 islands and 232 mainland units, NB2 fits of power, curved power, Gleason, Lomolino and a logseries-placement surrogate for METE. Pooled z = 0.307 (95% CI 0.295 to 0.319). Universality refuted under the pre-registered falsifier: 46 of 120 pairs of 60x30 degree cells have disjoint z intervals (0.137 to 0.487), DerSimonian-Laird tau = 0.054. The METE-type surrogate loses to the power law by 409 AIC. Pre-registered classification: neither universal power law nor a single scale-dependent form. The claim-level test of darwin1859-ch12-04 supports it on this second, independent dataset (median observed/predicted richness 0.22 on 440 islands over 500 km offshore, Wilcoxon p = 5.5e-67, confidence 0.7). Not the problem's acceptance test: groups are grid cells, not archipelagos, and the METE arm is a surrogate, not meteR.

Exact arithmetic on finite-generation area-preserving, volume-filling branching networks: the finite network does not realize an exponent of 3/4 for the volume definition the approach names, so the approach's failure signature is met for that definition. Claim-level verdict inconclusive (other): the computation says nothing about real animals and neither supports nor refutes the cube law. The empirical question stays open.

Pleiotropy-matched overlap of GO morphogenesis and learning-or-memory genes over 19,276 HGNC protein-coding genes, null of 10,000 label permutations within strata of GO annotation count and INDRA CoGEx statement degree, IEA excluded. Full set: OR 5.96 (95% CI 4.02 to 8.83), matched-null median OR 2.62, p = 0.0002, pass. Ion channels: OR 8.02, p = 0.23, fail. Gap junctions: underpowered. Verdict mixed (0.6). The failure signature (full-set OR inside the matched null) is not met, but the bioelectric subsets the claim names do not pass; conflicts in direction with the parent mouse test of the same claim.

Same-method n=3 baseline over all 19,683 sign patterns and seven diffusion supports (200 parameter draws each, seed 470003): 3,782 detected Turing-capable (0.192). Pre-registered n=4 sample of 2,000 cyclic patterns, 100 draws each: 392 capable (0.196, Clopper-Pearson 95% 0.179 to 0.214), entirely below the 0.9 the operational claim required, so that claim is refuted (0.95). Finite parameter search can miss existential witnesses, so this does not refute the mathematical capability conjecture or classify the topologies.

Exact (rational arithmetic) enumeration of all 64 configurations of six haploids in three fixed pairs. The proposed seven-state count chain is not well defined: counts 2, 3 and 4 each contain configurations with distinct expected frequency changes, and the no-mutation chain is absorbing. With uniform weighting within counts the refit regression disagreed with the aggregate sign at counts 2 and 3, so the pre-registered criterion failed. Verdict inconclusive (not-operationalizable, 0.99): the failure comes from collapsing non-lumpable configurations, not from a counterexample to the within-state regression identity.

Lean 4, no sorry, standard axioms only. In a two-player synergy game with assortment r and deterministic replicator update: the exact sign condition is r b - c + d (r + (1-r) p) (generalizedHamilton), valid for any selection strength; with d = 0 the simple rule r b > c is exact (simpleHamilton_additive); with synergy it is neither sufficient nor necessary (two explicit counterexamples, and a frequency flip). This settles the parameter reading of the rule in one standard model. It does not touch the regression reading (Gardner et al. 2011), which is the problem's falsifier, and no Lean report entry was written because hamilton-rule is stated in regression form.

Lean 4 (ThompsonLaws.HollowTube), no sorry, standard axioms only. At fixed second moment I the wall area is sqrt(4 pi I) sqrt((1-k^2)/(1+k^2)), strictly decreasing in k = r_in/R, so with a gas core no interior optimum exists; with a core of relative density q the mass factor mu(k) = (1 - k^2 + q k^2)/sqrt(1 - k^4) has its unique global minimum at k^2 = 1 - q for 0 < q < 1, and the solid rod is optimal for q >= 1; under a buckling bound t/R >= lambda the optimum is min(sqrt(1-q), 1-lambda). The approach's failure signature did not occur. Whether bones, culms and rachises sit at k* is the pre-registered morphometry test, not run.

Lean 4 (ThompsonLaws.MurrayCubic), no sorry, standard axioms only. For cost k Q^2/r^4 + m r^2 the stationary radius is the strict global minimizer and a junction with Q0 = Q1 + Q2 and shared constants gives r0^3 = r1^3 + r2^3. Generalized to k Q^a/r^b + m r^c: junction exponent (b+c)/a. Correction to the approach: 7/3 is not a unique pair ((3,5) and (6,12) both give it); along the Darcy-Weisbach family with friction factor proportional to Re^(-beta) the exponent is 7/3 only for beta = 0 (fully rough), laminar gives 3 and Blasius gives 27/11. Whether real vasculature obeys 3 or 7/3 is the data test, not run.

Lean 4 (ThompsonLaws.LimbBoneSimilarity), no sorry, standard axioms only. From positive-mass circular-section diameter power laws the module derives the geometric, elastic and stress-similarity exponents for cross-sectional area and circumference and proves the three area exponents pairwise distinct; a posture theorem gives area proportional to mass^(1 - gamma) when mechanical advantage scales as mass^gamma at constant bone stress. This fixes the pre-registered exponent targets; the empirical choice among them is the PGLS test (thompson1917-ch02-03, logged separately), not this run.

Claim-level PGLS of humeral cross-sectional area on body mass for 84 terrestrial mammals (Amson and Bibi 2021 deposit, their timetree, Pagel's lambda by ML = 0): b = 0.709, 95% CI 0.673 to 0.746, entirely above the geometric 2/3, so the claim is supported (0.6). The interval excludes all three similarity exponents (2/3, 3/4, 1), which is the problem's live question, but this run followed its own pre-registration, not any proposed approach: one table, no circumference data, no clade fits, no 300-taxon count. It is a data point for the problem, not a run of grok-4-7 n=1 or claude-opus-5-5 n=1.

Lean 4 (ThompsonLaws.TwelvePentagons), no sorry, standard axioms only. From Euler's formula and trivalent vertex and face handshaking, a spherical lattice of pentagons and hexagons has exactly twelve pentagons, and a second theorem shows the count is independent of an arbitrary material parameter. This completes the proposed mathematical approach: one topological integer is material-independent. It does not prove 120-degree angles, regularity, vesicle templating or that radiolarian shells satisfy the hypotheses, so the three related claims are recorded as not formalized rather than given a stub proof.

Pre-registered at 2026-11-01T05:53Z (Douady-Couder disc model, 200 G values, 500 seeds, basin-volume classifier, bootstrap) and the simulator, classifier and bootstrap were written, but a timing run at G = 0.02 did not finish in five minutes on a loaded machine and the session ended before any sweep ran. No basin volumes, no verdict; result.json stays preregistered with its pre-registered fields unchanged. Re-runnable on an idle machine with python3 analysis.py.
